messages.author: 30b37db3d992e3df
messages.subject: constructing replicate indices
parts:
Could I ask a few questions concerning the indices needed
to run an ar1 replicated model in a longitudinal setting?

The model will have for its random effects specification:

f(idx.ts, model="ar1",  replicate=idx.repl)

where idx.ts is an index of the time series, and idx.repl
is the index for the replicates. My questions concern how to
construct these two indices, given the structure of the data.
The story I have in mind is where I indivs are observed at T
times.

CASE 1 : the data is stacked by individuals, then by time.

Indiv      Time
=====   ====
1           1
1           2
1           3
2           1
2           2
2           3

In this case, I think that idx.ts is 1 2 3  1 2 3 ...
and idx.repl is 1 1 1  2 2 2 ...
Is this right?

CASE 2 - same data, but stacked by times, then indivs

Indiv      Time
=====   ====
1           1
2           1
3           1
1           2
2           2
3           2

In this case is idx.ts = 1 1 1   2 2 2 ...  and
idx.repl = 1 2 3   1 2 3  ... ? If not, what should
they be?

CASE 3 - Like case 1 except that indiv 2 is observed only
at times 1 and 3 (in this case I also show indiv 3):

Indiv      Time
=====   ====
1           1
1           2
1           3
2           1
2           3
3           1
3           2
3           3

Here I'm stumped. Should the idx.ts be 1 2 3  1 3   1 2 3 ...
and then idx.repl = 1 1 1   2 2  3 3 3  ...  or what?

Final question: am I correct that if the indivs and times
had been identified as 0,1,2 .. (instead of 1,2,3 ...) 
or the times as years (1990, 1991, ...) then
the indices in the f-specification must still start from 1? 
Or could they be zero-based or match the years?


Basically, I'm not sure I understand what the two indices
are supposed to be revealing. If anyone could set me
straight I'd be most grateful.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] constructing replicate indices
parts:
Hi,
From what I can see, you got it exactly right in all three cases!

As for 0-based indexing, or absolute years, I recommend converting to 1,2,3,... as in your case examples. This is required for the replicate indices to work as intended, and also for the main model indexing to be sure to work as intended (it’s a bit more complicated under the hood for some models, so sticking to the sure-to-work version is safer).

Finn
